validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real and genuinely proposed. This is FERC Docket PF13-17-000 (pre-filing, opened Aug 2013) -> CP14-101-000 (formal NGA sec.7(c) application filed 2014-03-07), 'Clarksville Natural Gas Interconnect Pipeline Project,' filed by the City of Clarksville, Tennessee (d/b/a Clarksville Gas and Water) to connect its municipal LDC system to Texas Gas Transmission, LLC's interstate mainline near Elkton, KY. Independently confirmed via: FERC's own Federal Register notices (pre-filing NOI 2013-24469, application notice 2014-06346, EA-availability notice 2014-15697), local press covering the same proposal from local opposition (Kentucky New Era and local3news.com, both Sept 30 2013) through the 2014-10 FERC approval (Clarksville Now) to the 2017-02 eminent-domain dispute (The Leaf-Chronicle), and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset, which tracked this exact project (docket CP14-101, 23 mi, 12-in, 52 MMcf/d, operator 'Clarksville Gas & Water Department') across 28 releases from 2018-05 (status Approved/On Hold) through the current 2026-08 release (status Cancelled since a 2021-04-27 update). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a Gas transmission-interconnect row -- an NGA sec.7(c) limited-jurisdiction certificate proceeding (interstate facilities only apply for one) confirms it is not a purely intrastate distribution extension. DUPLICATE: checked against all 41 rows in this batch's roster. P2509 'Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO)' is a wholly different pipeline/company (Enbridge's Texas Eastern, not Boardwalk's Texas Gas Transmission) despite the similar generic name -- no overlap. P5600 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline' (TGP NGL Conversion, 964 mi) is also a different company (Kinder Morgan's TGP) and a different kind of project (NGL conversion of an existing mainline) -- no overlap with this small (23 mi) lateral interconnect. No other roster row touches Todd County KY, Elkton, or Clarksville TN. STATUS/CANCELLATION: see status_reviews -- CancelledYear=2021 is corroborated by EIA's dated release history and remains uncontradicted through EIA's most recent (2026-08) release and a wholly separate, unrelated Jan-2026 FERC filing (docket not yet assigned at the time EIA's dataset was last touched) by the same city for a different, much smaller interconnect to a different supplier (Pennyrile Regional Energy Agency) -- which would be redundant if this project had ever been completed.
